# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

## PR Description

Closes #957
# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

## PR Description

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

## PR Description

Closes #957
# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

## PR Description

Closes #957
# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. ## PR Description

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Important finding: In scm.js, `inv` is declared inside the `try` block with `var inv = ...` — var hoists, so `inv` at the return statement is accessible (function scope), value undefined if exception occurred. OK, `inv ? inv.census : null` handles that.

But one issue: when `conversations.length === 0 && inv.threads.length === 0`, `rawThreads` stays `[]` and returns `rawThreads: null`, even if the GraphQL census has unresolved threads. Wait — inv.threads would be non-empty if GraphQL nodes exist and are notices. If all GraphQL threads are notices/resolved/bot... Actually buildFromGraphQL enumerates ALL non-notice nodes (including resolved ones, which get `resolved: true` but are still in enriched list, and bots). So threads.length only 0 when no GraphQL nodes and no conversations. Edge case OK.

Another subtle issue in scm.js: `rawThreads = inv.threads` reassigns the local var `rawThreads` that was declared `var rawThreads = []` — fine.

Wait, there's a mismatch with gitOps.writePRContext: the scm.js comment says "gitOps.writePRContext only serializes .threads — the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" but the gitOps diff ADDED census to pr_discussions_raw.json: `JSON.stringify({ threads: openThreads, census: rawThreads.census || null }...)`. So the scm.js comment is stale/contradictory with gitOps.js change. Actually the gitOps change serializes census into pr_discussions_raw.json — that IS the AC3 "same-source" carrying. So the scm.js comment claiming "the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" is now false. Documentation inconsistency — minor.

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Important finding: In scm.js, `inv` is declared inside the `try` block with `var inv = ...` — var hoists, so `inv` at the return statement is accessible (function scope), value undefined if exception occurred. OK, `inv ? inv.census : null` handles that.

But one issue: when `conversations.length === 0 && inv.threads.length === 0`, `rawThreads` stays `[]` and returns `rawThreads: null`, even if the GraphQL census has unresolved threads. Wait — inv.threads would be non-empty if GraphQL nodes exist and are notices. If all GraphQL threads are notices/resolved/bot... Actually buildFromGraphQL enumerates ALL non-notice nodes (including resolved ones, which get `resolved: true` but are still in enriched list, and bots). So threads.length only 0 when no GraphQL nodes and no conversations. Edge case OK.

Another subtle issue in scm.js: `rawThreads = inv.threads` reassigns the local var `rawThreads` that was declared `var rawThreads = []` — fine.

Wait, there's a mismatch with gitOps.writePRContext: the scm.js comment says "gitOps.writePRContext only serializes .threads — the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" but the gitOps diff ADDED census to pr_discussions_raw.json: `JSON.stringify({ threads: openThreads, census: rawThreads.census || null }...)`. So the scm.js comment is stale/contradictory with gitOps.js change. Actually the gitOps change serializes census into pr_discussions_raw.json — that IS the AC3 "same-source" carrying. So the scm.js comment claiming "the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" is now false. Documentation inconsistency — minor.

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Important finding: In scm.js, `inv` is declared inside the `try` block with `var inv = ...` — var hoists, so `inv` at the return statement is accessible (function scope), value undefined if exception occurred. OK, `inv ? inv.census : null` handles that.

But one issue: when `conversations.length === 0 && inv.threads.length === 0`, `rawThreads` stays `[]` and returns `rawThreads: null`, even if the GraphQL census has unresolved threads. Wait — inv.threads would be non-empty if GraphQL nodes exist and are notices. If all GraphQL threads are notices/resolved/bot... Actually buildFromGraphQL enumerates ALL non-notice nodes (including resolved ones, which get `resolved: true` but are still in enriched list, and bots). So threads.length only 0 when no GraphQL nodes and no conversations. Edge case OK.

Another subtle issue in scm.js: `rawThreads = inv.threads` reassigns the local var `rawThreads` that was declared `var rawThreads = []` — fine.

Wait, there's a mismatch with gitOps.writePRContext: the scm.js comment says "gitOps.writePRContext only serializes .threads — the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" but the gitOps diff ADDED census to pr_discussions_raw.json: `JSON.stringify({ threads: openThreads, census: rawThreads.census || null }...)`. So the scm.js comment is stale/contradictory with gitOps.js change. Actually the gitOps change serializes census into pr_discussions_raw.json — that IS the AC3 "same-source" carrying. ## PR Description

# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>

# gh-957: rework no-op loop: leg sees 2 threads while sweep counts 64 → starves whole queue (live dart#424, 7 legs/2h)

## Description

Live 2026-10-17 08:00–10:55Z, epam/dmtools-dart PR #424 (gh-389). The machine rework-looped **7 times in 2 hours** (10:54, 10:44, 10:22, 09:55, 09:46, 09:30, 09:16Z — plus more before), every leg 'success', zero merges. It consumed the dart machine's tick budget — 7 other PRs (#414, #417, #419, #420, #421, #423, #426) got nothing.

**Mechanism (two halves):**
1. **Context mismatch:** the sweep's thread-arm rule counts 64 open GraphQL review threads on #424 and arms `agent:rework` (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed` comments every cycle). But the rework leg's input context (`review_state.md`) surfaces only **2** items, both machine status notices — the leg concludes 'Review decision is NONE, nothing to fix' (quote from its 10:48Z response). So the leg can NEVER satisfy the arm condition.
2. **No-change rework cannot resolve threads:** the leg's safety rule refuses to resolve threads without code changes ('Threads were NOT resolved'). Correct intent against silent drops, but combined with (1) it makes the loop infinite: arm → no-op leg → threads stay open → re-arm.

**Required fixes:**
- The rework leg's thread list must come from the SAME source the arm rule counts (GraphQL reviewThreads isResolved=false), not from review_state.md — otherwise the two never agree.
- A rework leg that determines all open threads are addressed/invalid must be allowed to RESOLVE them with an explanatory reply per thread (audit: reply + resolve, with the rework run URL).
- Loop guard: N consecutive rework legs with zero pushed commits and zero resolved threads on the same head → stop re-arming, escalate (label + issue comment) instead of burning the machine.

Workaround applied manually by operator: bulk-resolved #424's open threads with an audit comment after verifying the leg's green test evidence.

Important finding: In scm.js, `inv` is declared inside the `try` block with `var inv = ...` — var hoists, so `inv` at the return statement is accessible (function scope), value undefined if exception occurred. OK, `inv ? inv.census : null` handles that.

But one issue: when `conversations.length === 0 && inv.threads.length === 0`, `rawThreads` stays `[]` and returns `rawThreads: null`, even if the GraphQL census has unresolved threads. Wait — inv.threads would be non-empty if GraphQL nodes exist and are notices. If all GraphQL threads are notices/resolved/bot... Actually buildFromGraphQL enumerates ALL non-notice nodes (including resolved ones, which get `resolved: true` but are still in enriched list, and bots). So threads.length only 0 when no GraphQL nodes and no conversations. Edge case OK.

Another subtle issue in scm.js: `rawThreads = inv.threads` reassigns the local var `rawThreads` that was declared `var rawThreads = []` — fine.

Wait, there's a mismatch with gitOps.writePRContext: the scm.js comment says "gitOps.writePRContext only serializes .threads — the census never leaks into pr_discussions_raw.json" but the gitOps diff ADDED census to pr_discussions_raw.json: `JSON.stringify({ threads: openThreads, census: rawThreads.census || null }...)`. So the scm.js comment is stale/contradictory with gitOps.js change. Actually the gitOps change serializes census into pr_discussions_raw.json — that IS the AC3 "same-source" carrying. ## PR Description

Closes #957
# gh-957: rework no-op loop guard

### What changed
The threads-rule rework arm (leg sees 2 threads while the sweep counts 64 → starves the queue) is now bounded both sides of the loop: `pushReworkChanges` records machine-authored empty-lap markers per leg close (GraphQL `reviewThreads` inventory is now the single census via the new `reviewThreadInventory.js`), and the SM arm (`arm_rework` + `restore_rework_arm`) withholds the arm at `noopLapMax` (default 2) no-op laps on the unchanged head — escalating the owner once per head (label + 🛑 comment). A lap that pushed or resolved anything, or a new head, resets the budget by construction.

### Key decisions
- New pure module `js/common/reworkLoopGuard.js` (marker build/parse, consecutive-noop count, withhold decision) — machine-author-gated, fail-closed with no configured identity
- New `js/common/reviewThreadInventory.js`: GraphQL `reviewThreads` first, `review_comments` fallback only when GraphQL is unavailable — leg input and threads-census now the same source
- `scm.js` exposes the inventory on `createScm` and returns it from `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData` (single fetch per PR, cached); `githubHelpers` embeds it in `pr_info.md` under a machine-gated marker; rework prompt declares that contract
- Lap markers use hidden `<!-- dmtools:rework-lap … -->` comments; escalation dedup is head-keyed (`<!-- dmtools:rework-loop-escalated … -->`), so repeated ticks stay quiet
- Guard binds the SM restore path too (`restoreReworkArm`), not just the fresh arm; `instructions/rework` documents the new contract (census source, never "no threads found", audit-resolve rep)
- `node_testRunner.js` gained `assert.doesNotThrow` for parity with the GraalJS harness

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3305 passed, 0 failed
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  LEG[rework leg close] --> PRP[js/pushReworkChanges.js]
  PRP --> INV[reviewThreadInventory: GraphQL reviewThreads]
  PRP --> LAP[reworkLoopGuard.buildLapMarker head/pushed/resolved]
  LAP -->|PR comment, machine-authored| GH[(GitHub PR)]
  SM[smAgent arm_rework / restore_rework_arm] --> COUNT[reworkLoopGuard: consecutive no-op laps on head]
  GH --> COUNT
  COUNT -->|below noopLapMax| ARM[agent:rework armed]
  COUNT -->|at cap, once per head| ESC[🛑 comment + rework-loop-escalated label]
  NEW[new head / progress lap] -.->|resets budget| COUNT
```

</details>
